newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil chief regrets LDP failure to cut taxes.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil chief regrets LDP failure to cut taxes.

text.p: Japan's oil industry chief expressed deep disappointment on Wednesday over the ruling party tax system panel's failure to support a reduction in taxes on oil products.
The oil industry has been lobbying for the abolition of various oil taxes, claiming they are imposing an unfair burden on consumers.
The ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) included the reduction of taxes on oil products as part of its campaign pledges in October's general elections.
However, the LDP tax panel failed to adopt major changes to oil taxes in its final set of proposals released on Wednesday.
The party proposal is expected to be approved as a government plan later this month.

Yuji Idemitsu, the chairman of the Petroleum Association of Japan (PAJ) said in a statement that the industry "is deeply disappointed...that no specific, appropriate measures are to be taken this time."
He said in the statement that the industry would continue to campaign against taxes on oil products.

More than half of Japan's gasoline retail price of about 100 to 105 yen per litre is gasoline tax. On top of that, Japanese drivers must also pay a sales tax, which is currently three percent, but due to raised to five percent on April 1.
On the same day, a separate government panel said Import tariffs on oil products would be reduced.
Traditionally tariffs on oil products are reduced when those on crude oil are cut, as drafted under a long-term programme.
